questions.question: Who was appointed as Attorney General for India from 1st October, 2022?

__
 
• **R. Venkataramani** was appointed as the Attorney General for India starting from 1st October, 2022.
 
• The Attorney General for India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President of India under Article 76(1) of the Constitution of India.
 
• R. Venkataramani succeeded K. K. Venugopal, who served as the Attorney General from July 2017 to September 2022.
 
• The appointment of the Attorney General is a significant event as it plays a crucial role in advising the government on legal matters and representing it in the highest court of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **R. Venkataramani** has a distinguished career in law with extensive experience in constitutional, civil, and criminal law.
 
• He has been practicing in the Supreme Court of India for several decades and has also served as a member of the Law Commission of India.
 
• The Attorney General’s term is typically for three years, but it can be extended or shortened at the discretion of the President.
 
• The Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India and can participate in the proceedings of the Parliament, though without the right to vote.
 
• The role of the Attorney General is vital in ensuring that the actions of the government conform to the law and constitution.

questions.question: Which five-year plan of India was introduced under the leadership of Indira Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan** of India was introduced under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.
 
• It spanned from **1969 to 1974**.
 
• The main objectives of this plan were **growth with stability** and **progressive achievement of self-reliance**.
 
• During this period, India faced several challenges, including droughts, food shortages, and a significant influx of refugees from East Pakistan (now Bangladesh).
 
• Key initiatives during this plan included the **Green Revolution** to increase agricultural productivity and measures to control inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indira Gandhi, the first and only woman Prime Minister of India, played a crucial role in shaping India's economic policies during her tenure.
 
• The Five-Year Plans are a series of centralized and integrated national economic programs, which were modeled after the Soviet Union's planning system.
 
• The Planning Commission of India was responsible for drafting and implementing these plans until it was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.
 
• The Fourth Plan also focused on the expansion of the public sector and aimed at reducing inequalities in income and wealth distribution.

questions.question: During ancient India in the Tamil region, ordinary ploughmen were known as ________.

__
 
• During ancient India in the Tamil region, ordinary ploughmen were known as **uzhavar**.
 
• The term **uzhavar** specifically referred to individuals who were involved in the agricultural activity of ploughing the fields.
 
• This was a significant occupation in the agrarian society of ancient Tamil Nadu, reflecting the importance of agriculture in sustaining the community.
 
• Other terms like **adimai** and **kadaisiyar** referred to different social classes or roles within the society.
 
• The **vellalar** were typically landowners or higher-status agriculturalists, distinguishing them from the ordinary ploughmen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Agriculture played a central role in the economy, and various terms were used to denote different roles and responsibilities within this sector.
 
• The **uzhavar** were essential to the agricultural process, ensuring the cultivation and production of crops that sustained the population.
 
• Understanding these historical terms provides insight into the social and economic fabric of ancient Tamil society.
 
• These terms are also reflected in ancient Tamil literature and inscriptions, providing a historical record of the agricultural practices and social organization of the time.

questions.question: Before ______, India was in the first stage of demographic transition.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1921**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Before **1921**, India was in the first stage of demographic transition.
 
• The first stage of demographic transition is characterized by high birth rates and high death rates, which result in a relatively stable population.
 
• In 1921, India experienced a significant demographic shift known as the "Year of the Great Divide," where the population growth rate started to increase due to a decline in death rates while birth rates remained high.
 
• This shift marked the transition from the first stage to the second stage of demographic transition, where the population begins to grow rapidly.
 
• The demographic transition model explains the transformation of countries from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as part of the economic development process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The demographic transition model is divided into four stages: the pre-industrial stage, the transitional stage, the industrial stage, and the post-industrial stage.
 
• During the transitional stage, improvements in healthcare, sanitation, and food supply lead to a decline in death rates.
 
• The decline in death rates without a corresponding decline in birth rates results in rapid population growth during the second stage.
 
• As countries continue to develop, they eventually reach the third stage, where birth rates begin to decline, leading to a slower rate of population growth.
 
• In the final stage, both birth and death rates are low, stabilizing the population size.

questions.question: The Right to Freedom includes the right to practice any profession, occupation, trade, or business under which articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 19-22**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Right to Freedom includes the right to practice any profession, occupation, trade, or business under **Articles 19-22** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 19 specifically provides for the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc., and includes the freedom to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
 
• This right ensures that citizens have the liberty to choose their employment and conduct business activities freely, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interest of the general public.
 
• These provisions are fundamental in ensuring economic freedom and personal liberty within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• Other rights under the Right to Freedom include protection against arbitrary arrest and detention, as well as the right to life and personal liberty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 19-22** are part of the fundamental rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These articles collectively ensure that citizens have essential freedoms and protections against state actions that may infringe upon their personal liberties.
 
• Article 19 guarantees six freedoms: speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses, ensuring no person is convicted of any offense except for violation of law in force at the time of the commission of the act.
 
• Article 21 ensures protection of life and personal liberty, stating that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
 
• Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, ensuring that individuals have rights such as being informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to consult a legal practitioner.
 
• These articles form the cornerstone of individual freedoms and uphold the democratic ethos of the country.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023?

II. It amends the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Both I and II** are correct statements regarding the Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023.
 
• The Bill was **introduced in Lok Sabha in August, 2023**.
 
• It seeks to **amend the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017**.
 
• The amendments are aimed at addressing various issues and improving the implementation of the CGST Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017** was enacted to make provisions for levy and collection of tax on intra-state supply of goods or services by the central government.
 
• The **GST** is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• The **amendments** to the CGST Act are periodically made to address operational issues and to bring clarity on various provisions.
 
• The **GST Council** is responsible for making recommendations to the Union and the States on important issues related to GST.
